To do well on Hacker News, post a on a Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday morning between 8 and 11 a.m. ET. Make sure people can try your product right away without having to sign up. Then, write a comment explaining how your product works, what was difficult about building it, and what you learned along the way.
Hacker News is different from most other platforms. Its users are highly technical and generally dislike marketing language. They will examine your product closely and tell you exactly what they think, which can be extremely helpful.
## First, consider whether your product is a good fit for Hacker News
Be honest with yourself because it may save you from disappointment. Hacker News tends to favor open-source products, self-hosted software, developer tools, and products that people can try immediately.
If your product is a business tool that requires users to book a demo, it may be more difficult to launch successfully on Hacker News.
## When to post on Hacker News
Post on a Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday between 8 and 11 a.m. ET. This is when more people are likely to be active on the site, giving your post a better chance of being seen.
Avoid posting on weekends or late at night unless your target audience is distributed around the world and active during those hours.
## Choose the right type of post
If you have something people can try, use a title such as **Show HN: I built [X]**.
Use **Ask HN** when you genuinely want to ask a question or request feedback. Do not disguise a product launch as a discussion because Hacker News users will notice.
## The first hour or two is very important
If your post receives meaningful engagement during the first hour or two, it may reach the Hacker News front page. Even a relatively small amount of genuine engagement can help your post gain visibility.
However, be careful. Hacker News does not allow users to ask others for upvotes, and its systems may detect coordinated voting. Your post could be removed or your account could be banned.
Instead, share the post with people who may genuinely find it interesting. Let them read it and decide for themselves whether they want to upvote it.
## Write a strong first comment
This is one of the most important things you can do.
Immediately after publishing your post, add a comment explaining how the product works, what was difficult about building it, why you built it, and what you learned.
Write honestly and technically, as though you are speaking to other builders. Hacker News users appreciate transparency and generally dislike promotional language.
## Make it easy for people to try your product
Hacker News users expect to be able to try your product right away. Make sure they can use it, test it, or provide feedback immediately.
On launch day, remove as many barriers as possible.
Hacker News users generally dislike waiting lists, newsletter gates, and pages that require them to request access. If your launch link takes visitors to a page where they cannot immediately try the product, you will probably lose many people who might otherwise have been interested.
## Respond to every comment
For the first two hours, respond to every comment, including negative ones.
This helps keep the discussion active and shows that you are engaged and genuinely care about people’s feedback. Even critical feedback can be extremely valuable, so treat it that way.
Avoid becoming defensive. Answer questions directly, acknowledge valid criticism, and explain your decisions honestly.
## Look at what has worked before
Before publishing your post, study successful Hacker News launches.
Look at how founders wrote their titles and first comments, presented their products, and responded to criticism. Use these launches as inspiration, but do not copy their wording.
## What to expect
If your post reaches the Hacker News front page, it may bring hundreds of visitors or signups in a single day. You may also earn a valuable backlink that remains live for years.
Even if your post does not reach the front page, you can still receive useful feedback from technical users.
Remember that one unsuccessful launch does not mean your product cannot succeed on Hacker News. You can try again later after making meaningful improvements or launching a substantially updated version.
## The short version
  * Post a **Show HN** on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday between 8 and 11 a.m. ET.
  * Make sure people can try your product immediately without unnecessary barriers.
  * Write a technical first comment explaining how your product works, what was difficult about building it, and what you learned.
  * Focus on earning genuine engagement during the first hour or two, but never ask people to upvote your post.
  * Respond to every comment during the first two hours.
  * Make sure your product is a good fit for Hacker News. Developer tools, open-source products, self-hosted software, and products people can try immediately tend to perform well.

## Frequently asked questions
**When is the best time to launch on Hacker News?**
Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday between 8 and 11 a.m. ET is generally a good time because more users are likely to be active.
**What is the difference between Show HN and Ask HN?**
Use **Show HN** to share something you have built that people can try. Use **Ask HN** when you genuinely want to ask the Hacker News community a question.
**Can I ask my friends to upvote my Hacker News launch?**
No. Hacker News does not allow coordinated voting or requests for upvotes. Doing so could cause your post to be removed or your account to be restricted.
**How many upvotes do I need to reach the Hacker News front page?**
There is no fixed number. Ranking depends on several factors, including how quickly the post receives genuine engagement.
**How much traffic can a Hacker News front-page launch bring?**
A successful front-page launch can bring hundreds or even thousands of visitors. The exact number of signups will depend on your product, audience, positioning, and signup process.
**What kinds of products perform well on Hacker News?**
Open-source products, self-hosted software, technical projects, developer tools, and products that people can try immediately often perform well on Hacker News.
